# A finite cap-budget cone for actual radial strictification

This note gives an exact finite criterion for a specified class of
strictification motions. It retains original caps, actual convex
fiber compatibility, fixed total mixed mass, and every selected
budget. For radially invariant or strictly full/empty traces,
the cap inequalities in the criterion are exact for the whole
constructed path. General proper oblique traces give a genuine
first-order criterion, with strict inequalities sufficient.

The criterion is not asserted feasible for arbitrary small-cap
covers. Its dual is a concrete obstruction to this radial
positive-first-order mechanism, not to every possible shape variation.

## 1. Exact finite encoding of compatibility

Let P be a finite lattice-complete subset of Z^n. Let K_z be
full-dimensional compact convex polytopes in R^d, compatible under
every anchored Minkowski interpolation. Fix any affine section
q(z); it need not pass through centroids or lie inside the fibers.
Center coordinates by x->x-q(z), and write

    h_z(u)=h_(K_z-q(z))(u), w_z=|K_z|>0.

For each nonvertex j, take all extreme points alpha of the compact
polytope of representations

    j=sum_z alpha_z z, sum_z alpha_z=1,
    alpha_z>=0, alpha_j=0.

There are finitely many. Representations with selfweight reduce
to these by deleting and renormalizing that weight.

Take a complete common refinement of the normal fans of the finitely
many centered polytopes, and choose one nonzero generator on each
of its rays. Its cones are pointed polyhedral cones; their rays
generate them. Every h_z is linear on each common cone.

For every extreme excluded-target representation and every selected
ray u, form

    G_e=h_j(u)-sum_z alpha_z h_z(u)>=0,
    (A_e)_z=1_(z=j) h_j(u)-alpha_z h_z(u).                (1)

Thus A_e is a row indexed by P. Retain in A only the rows with
G_e=0, called active rows. Repetitions may be discarded but do
not affect the criterion.

Nonnegativity or strict positivity on these finitely many rays
is equivalent to the corresponding support inequality in every
nonzero direction: on each common cone it is a linear function
of u. Taking convex combinations of the extreme representations
then controls every excluded-target representation. Compactness
on unit directions gives a uniform positive support margin when
all the finitely many ray inequalities are strict.

## 2. Volume coordinates and exact finite budget inequalities

For a vector sigma indexed by P, define, for sufficiently small
t>=0,

    r_z(t)=(1+t sigma_z)^(1/d),
    K_z(t)=q(z)+r_z(t)(K_z-q(z)).                           (2)

All radii are positive. Total mixed mass is exactly

    M(t)=sum_z w_z+t sum_z w_z sigma_z.                    (3)

For each active row in (1), its perturbed support gap satisfies

    G_e(t)=(t/d) A_e sigma+O(t^2).                         (4)

There are finitely many rows. Inactive rows retain their positive
gaps for sufficiently small t. Therefore

    A sigma>0                                             (5)

is a sufficient condition for an actual uniform compatibility
margin for every sufficiently small positive t. The resulting
convex hull has exactly the prescribed positive integer fibers,
and it has an open neighborhood of independent compatible
Hausdorff perturbations.

Consider original nonvertical caps H_i, with original trace
volumes c_iz=|K_z intersect H_i|. Assume that for each cap/fiber
pair either its boundary passes through (z,q(z)), or its trace
is strictly full or strictly empty. In the former case radial
dilation preserves its fraction; in the latter case the trace
pattern persists locally. Thus throughout a sufficiently small
path (2),

    mu_t(H_i)=sum_z c_iz+t sum_z c_iz sigma_z.              (6)

Let C be the matrix with entries c_iz. The exact finite
criterion is

    w.sigma=0, C sigma<=0, A sigma>0.                     (7)

Every solution gives fixed total mass, nonincreasing budgets
for all original selected caps, and strict actual compatibility.
It does not replace a shared cap by independently moving copies.
All matrices use actual cap masses and actual support functions.

Conversely, (7) is necessary for a path in these volume coordinates
whose active support gaps have strictly positive first derivatives
and whose budgets do not increase to first order. Zero derivative
on an active gap may permit a higher-order mechanism, which (7)
does not classify.

If A has no rows, the original array is already strictly compatible
at every excluded-target relation; sigma=0 suffices for the stated
open-neighborhood property. Positive-interior balls persist under
small Hausdorff changes of the full-dimensional finite fibers.

## 3. Exact dual obstruction

Suppose A has at least one row. Homogeneity allows A sigma>0
to be rescaled to A sigma>=1. Ordinary finite-dimensional Farkas
duality gives the following exact alternative:

Either (7) is feasible, or there exist

    alpha>=0, alpha!=0, beta>=0, eta in R,
    A^T alpha=C^T beta+eta w.                              (8)

To check signs, use the system

    -A sigma<=-1, C sigma<=0, w.sigma=0.

Its infeasibility certificate is
-A^T alpha+C^T beta+eta w=0 with -sum alpha<0, which is
precisely (8). Conversely multiplying (8) by any vector satisfying
(7) gives a strictly positive left side and a nonpositive right
side, a contradiction.

Thus a dual obstruction has nonnegative weights on actual tight
compatibility rows and on actual selected cap-volume rows, plus
one signed total-mass coefficient. No cap-cover or small-budget
assumption automatically rules out these certificates.

## 4. General proper oblique traces

For a general cap write its fiber inequality in centered
coordinates as

    u_i.(x-q(z))>=tau_iz,

where tau_iz is affine in z. Suppose each original trace is
proper, strictly full, or strictly empty; supporting traces with
positive face area are excluded from this differentiable statement.
Let

    S_iz=H^(d-1)(K_z intersect boundary H_i)/|u_i|

on proper traces and zero on strict full/empty ones. Directly
differentiating

    r^d |(K_z-q(z)) intersect {u_i.x>=tau_iz/r}|

at r=1 gives d c_iz+tau_iz S_iz. Hence along (2),

    (d/dt) mu_t(H_i) at 0
       =sum_z B_iz sigma_z,
    B_iz=c_iz+(tau_iz/d)S_iz.                              (9)

The sign of the section term is positive. Strict full/empty
traces agree with (6), and a through-section trace has tau_iz=0,
also agreeing with (6).

Consequently w.sigma=0, A sigma>0, and B sigma<0 are sufficient
for strict compatibility and strict decrease of every cap for
all sufficiently small positive t. If only B sigma<=0 holds,
it is a first-order condition; rows with zero derivative require
higher-order control. The corresponding weak first-order
feasibility has the dual (8) with B replacing C. This does not
upgrade that weak condition to exact budget nonincrease.

Coverage is tracked separately and precisely. If the original
caps cover the whole continuous fiber at every relevant base,
they continue to cover every array (2). This includes a positively
balanced concurrent group through q. If they only cover the
original bounded source, a sufficient alternative is a uniform
strict margin min_(z,x in K_z) max_i L_i(z,x)>0; compactness
then preserves coverage for small Hausdorff perturbations.
A closed cover with zero margin is not automatically preserved
by a body perturbation.

## 5. An actual dual calibration with covering complements

Take P={0,...,m-1}, m>=3, and every fiber equal to a body K
containing the origin in its interior, of volume V. For the
polyhedral criterion assume K is a polytope. Use the two strict
endpoint-isolating caps and their complementary halfspaces from
exact-endpoint-cap-budgets-obstruct-flat-strictification.md.
Their traces are strictly full/empty. They cover the source
(indeed each complementary pair covers all ambient space).

Their cap rows are

    C_0=V e_0, C_1=V e_(m-1),
    C_bar0=V(1-e_0), C_bar1=V(1-e_(m-1)).

Choose any common-fan ray u with h=h_K(u)>0 and, for every
interior j, its endpoint interpolation row

    A_j=h[e_j-(1-j/(m-1))e_0-(j/(m-1))e_(m-1)].

Every such row is active. With alpha_j=1/h, beta_bar0=beta_bar1
=m/(2V), all other beta zero, and eta=(1-m)/V, one obtains
exactly

    sum_j alpha_j A_j
       =1-(m/2)(e_0+e_(m-1))
       =C^T beta+eta w.                                   (10)

This is a concrete actual-geometry instance of the dual
obstruction. The complementary budgets are large, so (10)
does not refute a theorem for a cover consisting only of
below-target caps.

## 6. Nonincrease succeeds when only the small endpoint budgets remain

The same actual product array also supplies an explicit positive
calibration. Put

    phi_j=j(m-1-j), phi_bar=(1/m)sum_j phi_j,
    sigma_j=phi_j-phi_bar.

Then sum sigma_j=0, both endpoint values are -phi_bar<0, and
for every excluded-target representation

    sigma_j-sum_z alpha_z sigma_z
       =sum_z alpha_z(z-j)^2>0.                            (11)

Since h_K(u)>0 in every nonzero direction, (11) gives (5).
Thus (2) preserves total mass exactly, strictly lowers both
isolated endpoint budgets, and creates a strict compatibility
neighborhood. It bypasses the obstruction to preserving those
same two budgets exactly.

For a simplex K centered at its centroid, one may additionally
retain its d+1 canonical cylindrical caps. Their margins sum
to zero, so they cover every entire fiber. Their rows are
C_i=Gamma_d w, and their budgets remain exactly unchanged by
sum w_z sigma_z=0. This gives an explicit covered, nonincreasing
strictification, with the endpoint budgets decreasing and the
canonical budgets fixed.

Those canonical budgets are Gamma_d M, not the below-OC
threshold Gamma_d M/2 in integer dimension one. The example
therefore calibrates the criterion without claiming the missing
small-cover implication.
